recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. If HL7 wants to revise current publication-process ID enforcement, do that in the IG Publisher or publication guidance rather than by retrofitting FHIR-19297 into a core StructureDefinition invariant.
issue_request: The Published/Persuasive with Modification Jira asked that each HL7 balloted implementation guide have a unique ImplementationGuide.id after generic IDs such as "ig" caused possible collisions when multiple IGs were loaded into a FHIR server. The accepted resolution said it was good practice to base the ImplementationGuide.id on package identity, document that guidance, and update IGPublisher automation.
initial_application: The explicit Jira-linked application is commit cc2b93ea66, which changed the old in-repo IGPublisher to generate fixed IDs for HL7 published IGs from npmName and businessVersion and to warn other IGs when the ImplementationGuide.id did not match the generated value. No FHIR-19297-tagged StructureDefinition or ImplementationGuide narrative change was found, and the old IGPublisher source was later removed from this checkout when it moved to Maven.
additional_context: ImplementationGuide remains active in source/fhir.ini. Current source requires ImplementationGuide.packageId, describes it as globally unique, and says HL7/FHIR Foundation package IDs are assigned by the FHIR product director. The current packages page also says NPM FHIR packages should contain an ImplementationGuide URL ending in packageId and that package names are globally unique. Later Zulip discussion supports a tooling-predictability rationale for the id/package warning while showing publication-process nuance around id, packageId, canonical URL, and approval documents.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Adding a core Resource.id constraint or broad normative statement would overstate the Jira resolution and risk conflicting with later publication-process nuance; current FHIR core source conveys the stable package-level uniqueness rule and the historical enforcement lives outside the current build source.

related_jiras.note: US Core raised the same generic-resource-id loading problem but was a FHIR-us-core issue with its own resolution, so it was not decided in this FHIR-core reconciliation.
